summary.text: A neonate was born at 24 + 1 week’s gestation weighing 650 g, started on CPAP in the NICU, received one dose of surfactant, caffeine for apnoea of prematurity and 36 hours of antibiotics stopped after negative blood cultures.

By DOL 7 he tolerated fortified expressed breast milk, then on DOL 8 deteriorated with abdominal distention, feed intolerance and more apnoeic episodes, was intubated and placed nil by mouth; abdominal x-ray findings were consistent with aerophagia while NEC and sepsis were suspected. X-rays by DOL 10 and on DOL 12 showed abnormal gas patterns and free air indicating perforation, and at 25 + 6 weeks corrected gestation he had resection of necrotic ascending colon and the ileocaecal valve with a double enterostomy.

Post-operatively he had acute kidney injury with hypotension requiring inotropic support, significant wound dehiscence, prolonged ventilation with failed extubations, and was extubated to CPAP on POD 36 after dexamethasone. He gained only 50 g from POD 2 to day 41 with high enterostomy output of 40–50 mls/kg/day, relying on parenteral nutrition and electrolyte infusions.

After work-up and contrast imaging of the distal bowel, automated chyme reinfusion therapy was started at DOL 53 (POD 41) weighing 1150 g, progressed from half to full volume, intravenous replacement of enterostomy losses was stopped and he had his first bowel movement within 48 hours. A Cot Card ended incorrect distal tubing placement, gastric feeds reached full fortified EBM feeds in 14 days, growth normalised and parenteral nutrition ceased.

Parents learned to manage his refeeding care. A distal limb prolapse brought re-anastomosis forward and on DOL 111 (40 weeks corrected, 2900 g) he returned to surgery after 58 days on the device with a 1750 g total gain, followed by a routine recovery with six days nil by mouth and return to full enteral feeds in three days.
